sourceDefectsObserved.observation: The three return points of claimRegionalRehome construct RegionalRehomeAttempt differently: the fresh-candidate path (line 5329) returns `{...claimed, sendAttempts: 1}` where `claimed` is the object built in startRegionalRehomeCandidate; the retry path (5192) and redrain path (5262) instead mutate and return the raw SQL row via `regionalRehomeAttempt(retry)` / `regionalRehomeAttempt(redrain)` after incrementing `send_attempts` in-place on the JS object (not re-reading it from the DB). This is not a bug given the DB write happened in the same statement, but it is a structural asymmetry: one path constructs a typed object from scratch, two paths mutate a raw SqlRow and coerce it through the row-shaped `regionalRehomeAttempt()` mapper.
sourceDefectsObserved.classification: intended-correction-candidate, not a confirmed defect -- functionally consistent, only a code-shape inconsistency worth flagging for a future refactor, not a parity gap.

sourceDefectsObserved.observation: When an existing assignment is forcibly reassigned (dead cell or stranded host), ALL activity leases for the identity are deleted (line 916-920) before the new target reservation is computed. This deliberately discards any lease accounting the identity held, including leases whose `cell_id` might not have been the stale source (though in practice only the source cell should hold leases at this point). No assertion in the read source verifies leases are scoped to the source cell_id before this blanket delete.
sourceDefectsObserved.classification: explicit-source-behavior, not a defect -- the comment at line 912-915 states the rationale directly (fenced/dead incarnation and stranded-host leases are the loop's own unclaimed artifacts); flagged only because the blanket DELETE has no defensive WHERE cell_id = sourceCellId guard, so any accounting bug upstream that left a lease on the wrong cell would be silently erased rather than surfaced.

sourceDefectsObserved.observation: changeActivity uses `adjustCellReservationAtomically` (a single conditional UPDATE...RETURNING, no separate cell-row lock) while acquireActivity uses explicit `lockCellRows`/`adjustCellReservationAtomically` with comments about lock ordering. changeActivity never locks the assignment row's cell explicitly before adjusting the cell reservation -- it relies entirely on adjustCellReservationAtomically's atomic conditional UPDATE to avoid a race, which is a different concurrency strategy from the explicit-lock-then-write pattern used everywhere else in the file (assign, acquireActivity, activateControl).
sourceDefectsObserved.classification: intended-correction-candidate -- appears to be a deliberate lighter-weight path for changeActivity (likely because it does not need cross-cell atomicity, only a single-cell conditional check), not a defect, but it is the one write path in the file that does not follow the dominant explicit-lock convention documented in the file's own comments (e.g. line 6958-6960).

operations.ownedState: Three mutually exclusive candidate classes tried in strict priority order inside one transaction: (1) retry -- an existing attempt with no drain receipt yet, <10 send attempts, cooling down 30s between sends; (2) redrain -- a RECEIPTED attempt whose drain_grace_ms window has elapsed but still shows an active source-cell lease, capped at REGIONAL_REHOME_REDRAIN_SEND_LIMIT=20 sends and spaced REGIONAL_REHOME_REDRAIN_INTERVAL_MS=60s apart; (3) fresh candidate -- up to 10 eligible (asia-east2-preferring, us-central1-resident, protocol>=1) hosts scored by observed_at ascending, each individually evaluated by startRegionalRehomeCandidate which performs the FULL migration-start side effects (assignment bump, activity leases, connection reservation, migration+incarnation rows, and a NEW relay_region_rehome_attempts row) inline.
operations.authFencing: Global gate: relay_region_rehome_control.enabled must be 1 and not_before <= now, re-checked TWICE (once unlocked outside the transaction as a fast no-op path, once locked inside). Worker-state gate: paused_until/next_dispatch_at must both be <= now. Fleet-safety gate: regionalRehomeSafetyAllowsClaim is checked BEFORE the retry/redrain SQL selects run (against the fast unlocked fleet snapshot) AND AGAIN with a FRESH LOCKED snapshot immediately before actually claiming a retry or redrain candidate -- a safety regression detected between the two checks aborts the claim by disabling the control (pauseRegionalRehomeForSafety) rather than silently proceeding. Fresh-candidate path additionally re-verifies the SPECIFIC preference row is still fresh/asia-east2, no OTHER active migration exists, source is general+us-central1+live+fresh+protocol>=1+incarnation-matched, source safety is 'clean' (regionalRehomeCellSafetyIsClean: fresh safety row matching runtime incarnation, sql failures/reconnects under limits, zero control-activity-recovery-failures, no pool pressure), source control lease is genuinely active (post-restart-safe via updated_at>=started_at), and picks the LEAST-LOADED clean target with sufficient reservation AND connection headroom among asia-east2 candidates.
operations.errorTaxonomy: This method NEVER throws to its caller for ordinary contention: the whole transaction body is wrapped in `.catch` that swallows ONLY isDatabaseLockUnavailable (logs candidatesTotal-candidatesFinished as 'busy', returns null) and rethrows everything else. Individual candidate rejection is recorded as a structured 'skip' reason (candidate_stale/source_ineligible/source_unclean/source_control_inactive/target_unclean/no_eligible_target/no_target_headroom) rather than an exception, aggregated and logged ONCE per tick (not per candidate) via aggregateRegionalRehomeCandidateSkips.
operations.transactionRaceRetry: Single transaction per call (called once per second by the worker); NO retry-on-lock-unavailable wrapper here (unlike assign/evacuation methods) -- a contended tick is simply abandoned wholesale (all remaining untried candidates in that tick are lost, to be re-evaluated fresh on the NEXT tick one second later), an explicit design tradeoff documented in the comment at line 5095-5096 ('a Postgres transaction is unusable after a NOWAIT abort').
